properties.title: G-Net: a Recurrent Network Approach to G-Computation for Counterfactual Prediction Under a Dynamic Treatment Regime

membership.reason: G-Net is a recurrent g-computation world model simulating Monte Carlo counterfactual patient trajectories under dynamic time-varying treatment strategies.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L3 counterfactual/branching dynamic-treatment-regime world model (WT_PHYSIOLOGY, BP_COMPARE).

properties.backbone: LSTM sequential g-computation state r_t + sequential conditional covariate/outcome heads

properties.flow: Observed history H_m + dynamic treatment policy g -> Monte Carlo LSTM g-computation rollouts -> counterfactual outcome trajectories

properties.purpose: Counterfactual outcome-trajectory estimation under competing dynamic time-varying treatment strategies.
properties.environment: In silico CVSim cardiovascular and pharmacokinetic tumor-growth simulators

assertions.rationale: Recurrent LSTM hidden representation r_t summarizing covariate and treatment history.
Conditioned on full patient history H_m.

Evaluated matched counterfactual trajectories under competing treatment strategies from identical observed histories: CVSim dynamic strategies gc1 vs gc2 starting at t=34 (Figures 3, 5, 6) and four counterfactual cancer-growth regimes (no treatment, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, both; Table 2), verified against known simulator counterfactual ground truth.
Multi-step Monte Carlo forward simulation under treatment strategy g.
Simulates future covariates and outcomes conditioned on dynamic and static treatment decisions A_t, evaluated across CVSim (gc1, gc2) and PK tumor-growth regimes (Figures 5-6, Table 2).
Monte Carlo trajectory sampling with empirical simulation noise.

Evaluated multi-step counterfactual rollout accuracy against simulator ground truth: 32-step RMSE (t=35..66) across 18 covariates on CVSim (Figures 5-6) and 1- to 4-step percent RMSE on tumor volume (Table 2, where LSTM-based G-Net outperforms CRN and R-MSN across all four treatment strategies).
Comparing competing dynamic treatment regimes in longitudinal clinical decision-making.
Counterfactual trajectory accuracy against ground-truth simulated dynamic regimes in CVSim and PK tumor simulator.

evidence_fragments.content: G-Net instead adopts a recurrent neural network framework to capture complex temporal and nonlinear dependencies in the data.

Figure 1: The G-Net: A flexible sequential deep learning framework for g-computation. Let Yt(g) denote the counterfactual outcome that would be observed at time t had, possibly contrary to fact, treatment strategy g been followed from baseline (Robins, 1986).
Figure 3: Covariate trajectories for the same patient under two different treatment strategies: gc1 (blue) and gc2 (orange) starting at t = 34 (black dashed line).

The estimated and actual population-level average trajectories under gc1 and gc2 from the CVSim data set for one of the selected variable, AP (arterial pressure), are plotted in Figure 6. The plot shows that LSTM-based models outperform GLMs and more accurately predict counterfactual population AP trajectories.

locator.section_or_table: Section 4 Comparison with R-MSN & CRN & Table 2

evidence_fragments.content: To evaluate model performance, we generated four test sets in which various counterfactual regimes (static, as R-MSNs can only estimate counterfactuals under static regimes) were followed for the final four time points in the test set: give only radiotherapy, only chemotherapy, both chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and no treatment.

capability_assessments.rationale: LSTM-based sequential g-computation simulating Monte Carlo counterfactual trajectories under dynamic time-varying treatment policies (L3).

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R0 In silico physiological simulator validation

limitations: Evaluated solely on in silico CVSim and PK tumor simulators; relies on sequential exchangeability and positivity assumptions.
notes: All 18 physical PDF pages extracted/read; page 4 visually inspected via rendered PNG.

legacy_cells.B: G-Net: a Recurrent Network Approach to G-Computation for Counterfactual Prediction Under a Dynamic Treatment Regime
legacy_cells.C: Rui Li, Stephanie Hu, Mingyu Lu, Yuria Utsumi, Prithwish Chakraborty, Daby M. Sow, et al.
legacy_cells.O: Simulated cardiovascular/hemodynamic trajectories; non-small cell lung cancer tumor-growth trajectories
legacy_cells.S: Given observed patient history, what future covariate/outcome trajectories are predicted under specified alternative dynamic treatment strategies?
legacy_cells.T: Simulated cardiovascular patients initialized with physiological parameter values; simulated tumor-growth patients in a pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic model; no clinical cohort
legacy_cells.U: Physicians/clinicians considering alternative treatment strategies (described as a potential use)
legacy_cells.V: Compare predicted patient outcomes under specified future treatment strategies
legacy_cells.AI: Tabular time-series: continuous and categorical clinical/hemodynamic covariates, treatment histories/doses, and tumor volume/treatment variables
legacy_cells.AJ: LSTM recurrent history representation in LSTM variants; conditional covariate estimators implemented as linear models, MLPs, or LSTMs
legacy_cells.AS: 32-dimensional representation hidden state in the selected CVSim LSTM3 configuration
legacy_cells.BD: Fluid dose in mL; vasopressor dose (unit not stated); chemotherapy and radiation treatment variables/doses
legacy_cells.BF: Dynamic treatment rules use observed history, including MAP thresholds and pulmonary-edema status; dose depends on MAP/CVP deviations from stated targets
legacy_cells.BL: CVSim trajectories have 66 time steps; counterfactual predictions cover steps 35–66 (32 steps); physical interval not stated
legacy_cells.BN: G-computation factorization of conditional covariate distributions; explicit causal ordering of covariates, treatment, and outcome
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted future covariate trajectories and outcomes, including hemodynamic variables (e.g., MAP/AP) and tumor volume
legacy_cells.BV: Train conditional estimators to predict covariates at each time point using gradient descent and teacher forcing; exact loss formula not specified in main text
legacy_cells.CA: CVSim experiments used NVIDIA Tesla V100 SXM2 GPUs; tumor-growth experiments used NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPU with 12 vCPUs and 110 GB memory
legacy_cells.CD: 32 time steps (CVSim; prediction from t=35 to t=66)
legacy_cells.CG: 100 Monte Carlo trajectory simulations per patient in the CVSim experiments
legacy_cells.CV: Consistency; sequential exchangeability/no unobserved confounding; positivity
legacy_cells.CX: Validated against known counterfactual ground truth generated by two simulators: CVSim/S-CVSim and a tumor-growth PK-PD simulation
legacy_cells.DN: CVSim (modified as S-CVSim); simulated tumor-growth data based on a pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic model
legacy_cells.DQ: CVSim: 12,000 observational trajectories (10,000 training, 2,000 validation) and 851 retained trajectories per counterfactual test regime; tumor simulation: 10,000 training, 1,000 validation, and 1,000 test trajectories
legacy_cells.DY: Tumor-growth no-treatment percent RMSE at horizons t=1–4: G-Net LSTM1 0.25, 0.47, 0.72, 1.01; LSTM2 0.25, 0.47, 0.70, 0.94; LSTM3 0.28, 0.54, 0.83, 1.20
legacy_cells.EB: Simulated outcomes changed under alternative treatment regimes; CVSim examples show different predicted MAP effects under gc1 versus gc2 for patients with similar initial MAP histories
legacy_cells.EI: Compared G-Net with GLM and MLP g-computation baselines; LSTM variants had lower counterfactual RMSE than GLM, while MLP counterfactual RMSE was 1.03–1.80 and substantially higher
legacy_cells.EJ: On simulated tumor growth, compared with R-MSN and CRN; G-Net LSTM variants outperformed both across all four tested treatment strategies
legacy_cells.EK: Compared identity/pass-through versus LSTM history representations and linear, MLP, and LSTM conditional estimators; LSTM history representation improved counterfactual prediction over GLM/MLP alternatives in reported settings
legacy_cells.EL: MLP models had better one-step validation loss than GLM but unstable and much worse counterfactual trajectory RMSE (1.03–1.80); authors caution against extrapolating too far beyond observed treatment strategies
legacy_cells.FL: G-Net forms a recurrent representation of observed covariate and treatment history, then uses ordered conditional estimators for covariate groups to produce one-step predictions; repeated sampling under specified treatment strategies yields multi-step counterfactual trajectories. No planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces a recurrent-network framework for g-computation under dynamic time-varying treatment strategies, provides flexible sequential representations/conditional estimators, and evaluates it on two simulated settings with known counterfactual ground truth.
legacy_cells.FN: In CVSim, LSTM-based G-Net variants outperformed GLM on counterfactual RMSE over time. In tumor-growth simulation, G-Net LSTM variants outperformed CRN and R-MSN for all four tested strategies; LSTM1 had the best overall RMSE in three of four datasets.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors caution that flexible models may extrapolate poorly to counterfactual strategies far from the observed data and may not outperform alternatives without nonlinear or long-term dependencies. Their Monte Carlo uncertainty omits uncertainty in network parameter estimates.
legacy_cells.FP: Quantify model-parameter uncertainty, investigate alternative history-representation architectures, and evaluate G-Net on real-world data for sequential treatment decision-making in critical care.
legacy_cells.FQ: Prior g-computation implementations mainly used classical regression models with limited ability to capture complex temporal and nonlinear dependencies; earlier deep approaches did not handle dynamic treatment strategies as addressed here.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is limited to simulator-generated trajectories with known counterfactual ground truth. The paper does not demonstrate real-patient validation, prospective clinical benefit, or an implemented decision-making/planning loop.
